svg.title: Where the NB-IoT carrier lives
svg.text: Where the carrier lives: Band 8, a 180 kHz block, and one frequency for every cell
Telkomsel 900 MHz block (15 MHz of downlink)
Band 8 downlink, 925–960 MHz (the tower transmits here)
which block belongs to whom: my reading of public data;
the carrier itself says MCC 510 / MNC 10 = Telkomsel
subcarrier number k = 0 … 11, centred at (k − 5.5) × 15 kHz: no subcarrier sits exactly on 935.4 MHz
Frequency reuse 1: every Telkomsel NB-IoT cell transmits on the same 935.4 MHz
Older networks give neighbouring cells different frequencies (reuse 3, 4, 7…).
NB-IoT has only 180 kHz to work with, so Telkomsel gives every cell the same carrier.
What keeps them apart is the cell ID (PCI, 0–503). It changes:
• the NSSS sequence (how a receiver learns which cell it hears),
• where the reference signals (NRS) sit in the grid (PCI mod 6),
• the scrambling codes on the broadcast and data channels.
Signals from other cells still arrive on top of mine, as interference.
They hit hardest where every cell transmits at the same moment: subframe 0
(NPBCH, every cell, every frame) and subframe 4 (SIB1). Part 13 shows it in my data.
